Issued at 301 PM CDT Mon Oct 5 2026

SYNOPSIS:

A mid-level ridge was located over the northern Plains and 
Canadian Prairies this afternoon with a closed upper low over 
northern Quebec. A shortwave trough was found east of the 
Rockies from the Nebraska Panhandle to northern Alberta. A 
second trough was positioned over southern Manitoba and the 
eastern Dakotas. A broad area of isentropic ascent aloft 
supported and area of stratus and cumulus clouds over central 
Minnesota into portions of eastern North Dakota. At the surface 
developing low pressure was found over central Saskatchewan with
a serpentine warm front which extended south over eastern 
Montana and southwest North Dakota then east across northern 
South Dakota.

TONIGHT:

The surface warm front will lift northeastward across Minnesota
and northwest Wisconsin by 7 AM Tuesday as the shortwave 
troughs propagate eastward. Persistent isentropic ascent north 
of the warm front will support scattered shower development over
west-central Minnesota initially expanding and moving eastward 
into central and portions of northeast Minnesota by this 
evening. 05.18Z RAP analysis reveals a bubble of <= 700 J/kg of 
MUCAPE over southeast North Dakota and west-central Minnesota. 
That area of meager instability will propagate northeastward 
across central and portions of northeast Minnesota this 
afternoon and evening. A few weak thunderstorms are possible in 
that area. A 25-35 kt south-southwesterly low-level jet over 
eastern South Dakota this afternoon will advance northeastward 
this evening and will strengthen to 25-45 kt overnight. South of
the surface warm front momentum transfer may be sufficient to 
generate wind gusts of 15 to 20 mph over the Brainerd Lakes and 
east into northwest Wisconsin. Rain amounts from the showers 
will generally be between a trace and a tenth of an inch. Some 
spots may pick up as much as two tenths of an inch. Areas along 
and north of a line from Pine River to Grand Marais will likely 
stay dry. Showers and perhaps a few storms will move out of 
northwest Wisconsin Tuesday morning. A few spots in the eastern 
Arrowhead may see frost develop if skies can remain clear.

TUESDAY AND TUESDAY NIGHT:

Skies will clear from west to east during the day and 
temperatures will trend warmer in the wake of the warm front. 
Look for highs Tuesday to reach the middle 60s to middle 70s, 
around 10-15 degrees above normal. Gusty southerly winds are 
expected over northwest Wisconsin into the I-35 corridor of 
Minnesota as the low-level jet gradually weakens and pushes 
eastward during the day. Gusts of 15-25 mph are expected with 
the highest values east of a Hayward to Bayfield line.

A cold front will advance southeastward across northern 
Minnesota into northwest Wisconsin by early Tuesday evening. 
Winds will veer northwesterly behind the cold front and will 
gradually weaken during the evening. Low temps will be in the 
upper 30s to middle 40s.

WEDNESDAY THROUGH FRIDAY NIGHT:

Northwest flow is forecast in the wake of Tuesday's cold front.
Temperatures will cool slightly while remaining several degrees
above normal. Diurnal shower chances are expected as colder air
aloft advects east-southeast over the Northland. Highs will be 
in the low 60s to near 70 on Wednesday then upper 50s to middle 
60s Thursday and Friday.

SATURDAY INTO EARLY NEXT WEEK:

A more unsettled pattern takes shape Saturday into early next 
week. Guidance indicates an upper-level ridge will move into the
northern Plains and Canadian Prairies Friday night and Saturday
morning. A low pressure system is forecast to develop over 
eastern Montana and ride northeastward toward James Bay by 
Sunday morning. That progression will pull another warm front 
northward across the region with temperatures climbing well 
above normal for Saturday. Light rain showers are possible ahead
of the front Saturday. A cool front will follow on Sunday and 
will stall out over the Upper Midwest Sunday night and Monday 
leaving a baroclinic zone in place across Minnesota and 
Wisconsin. Widespread shower chances are forecast Sunday through
Tuesday.
